method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: Neonatal Lupus and Congenital Heart Block
topic.coverageNote: Same open review is used for catalogue 1934 with different questions. ACR 2020 reproductive-health guideline PMIDs in the spreadsheet did not resolve to that paper in Europe PMC.

mcqs.question: In anti-Ro/SSA and/or anti-La/SSB pregnancies with no prior neonatal lupus, about what proportion develop third-degree heart block?

options.D: It does not occur without a prior affected child
options.E: Only anti-dsDNA pregnancies are at risk

mcqs.explanation: The review states third-degree block occurs in about 2% of anti-Ro/SSA and/or anti-La/SSB pregnancies without a prior history of neonatal lupus.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association
sourceRefs.excerpt: Third-degree heart block occurs in about 2% of anti-Ro/SSA and/or anti-La/SSB antibody-associated pregnancies without a prior history of NLS.

mcqs.question: After a child with cutaneous or cardiac neonatal lupus, what recurrence risk for third-degree block does the review give?

options.E: Zero if the mother takes aspirin

mcqs.explanation: After cutaneous or cardiac neonatal lupus, the risk of third-degree block in a subsequent pregnancy is about 13–18%.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association
sourceRefs.excerpt: Following cutaneous or cardiac NLS, the risk of third-degree heart block in a subsequent pregnancy increases significantly and ranges between 13% and 18%.

mcqs.question: Which statement about complete heart block in neonatal lupus matches the review?

options.A: It is usually transient and resolves without pacing
options.B: It tends to be permanent and is among the most severe complications
options.C: It occurs only with anti-Sm antibodies
options.D: It is prevented by delivery before 28 weeks in all cases
options.E: It is a postnatal infection, not an antibody-mediated injury

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It tends to be permanent and is among the most severe complications
mcqs.explanation: Third-degree heart block is described as one of the most severe complications and tends to be permanent.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association
sourceRefs.excerpt: heart block is one of the most severe complications and tends to be permanent.

mcqs.question: What fetal mortality range does the review associate with neonatal lupus?

options.D: Mortality is limited to cutaneous disease
options.E: The review states mortality has not been estimated

mcqs.explanation: Fetal mortality associated with neonatal lupus is given as 15–20%, related to complications such as hydrops and cardiomyopathy.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association
sourceRefs.excerpt: There is significant fetal mortality associated with NLS, ranging from 15% to 20%.

mcqs.question: What surveillance point does the review make about fetal echocardiography?

options.A: It can detect first-degree through complete block but cannot predict progression to complete block
options.C: It is useful only after birth
options.D: A single scan at 12 weeks excludes later block
options.E: It is contraindicated because of Doppler heating

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It can detect first-degree through complete block but cannot predict progression to complete block
mcqs.explanation: Fetal echocardiography can detect the range from first-degree to complete heart block, but the review says it cannot predict progression to complete block.

sourceRefs.sourceBody: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association
sourceRefs.excerpt: FEC can detect the full range of heart block including first-degree heart block to complete heart block. Although FEC cannot predict the progression to complete heart block, it remains a sensitive tool for early detection of heart block.
